sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Rockwall?
sections.html:
The Rockwall Central Appraisal District both values property and collects the tax. Rockwall County's own tax office page says that since October 1, 2012, all county property taxes and their collection have been handled by the appraisal district, so an owner receives a single bill listing every entity.

The district sits at 841 Justin Road in Rockwall and answers at 972-771-2034. Its website hosts tax statements at a separate payment portal, and it reported that 2026 statements were mailed the week of October 12. The same site posts a notice of the local property tax database, where you can look up each taxing unit's proposed and adopted rate for your parcel.

Because one office handles both jobs, a question about value and a question about a payoff can go to the same counter. It also means a seller can ask for one statement that shows the city, county, school and any special district balances together.

sections.h2: What is the Rockwall city tax rate?
sections.html:
The city council sets its rate each September, so read the current figure in the truth-in-taxation database or ask city finance for the adopted number. The database is linked from the appraisal district and lists every unit that taxes your address.

Rockwall County's tax office page also links a five-year history of tax rates under its truth-in-taxation information. That history is the quickest way to see whether the city, the county and the school district have been moving up or down.

sections.h2: What dates and penalties apply to a Rockwall tax bill?
sections.html:
The appraisal date is January 1, and bills go out in October. Pay by January 31, because anything unpaid on February 1 is delinquent. A late bill picks up a six percent penalty plus one percent interest right away.

After that the penalty climbs by one percent each month until it hits 12 percent on July 1, while interest keeps adding one percent a month with no ceiling. Taxing units that contract with a collection lawyer may tack on up to 20 percent. You may be able to ask for a waiver of penalty and interest if you pay within 21 days of learning about the delinquency and request it in writing within 181 days of the delinquency date.

  • Split payments: first half by November 30, second half by June 30.
  • Seniors and disabled owners may use four installments.
  • Homestead owners can sometimes spread old taxes over as many as 36 months.

The Comptroller's payment guide explains each option.

sections.h2: How do I file a homestead exemption or protest in Rockwall?
sections.html:
File through the appraisal district, and file before May 1 for the general homestead exemption. The district warns on its home page that filing a homestead exemption is free and that anyone charging a fee to file the paperwork should be avoided.

A protest is due by May 15 or 30 days after the notice of appraised value is delivered, whichever is later. The district says review board hearings typically run on weekdays from April through July. If you want to appear by phone or video, the district requires a notarized affidavit before you can present or discuss evidence. Bring comparable sales within your own neighborhood, since county-wide medians say little about one street.

The state exemption amounts are the same everywhere in Texas: $140,000 for school district taxes on a homestead, and $60,000 more for owners 65 or older or disabled. Local governments may add their own. The district posts an exemption breakdown that lists the local figures, and it is worth reading before you file.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Rockwall owners?
sections.html:
Rockwall is mostly owner-occupied, with 72.5 percent of homes lived in by their owners and 18,273 households averaging 2.78 people. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $2,542, and those without one report $954, for 2020-2024.

  • 15.8 percent of residents are 65 or older, so the senior exemption and tax freeze apply to a meaningful share of owners.
  • The Census counts 2,539 veterans, some of whom may qualify for a disabled veteran exemption.
  • 86.0 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so listings turn over slowly.

These are citywide medians, and prices differ between lakeside streets and older neighborhoods near the square.

sections.h2: Why does Rockwall's land and lake setting matter to a sale?
sections.html:
Rockwall County is the smallest county in Texas at 147 square miles, and Rockwall is its seat, about 25 miles northeast of Dallas. The county sits on the Blackland Prairie, and the Texas State Historical Association notes its soils have cracking clayey subsoils. Foundation movement is a common inspection topic on clay ground, so a seller who has a foundation report on file is better prepared.

Lake Ray Hubbard, built in 1969 and 1970 to supply Dallas, now covers 13.55 percent of the county. Interstate 30 crosses the county from the Dallas County line toward Royse City, which is why so many residents commute. The Census puts the mean trip to work at 31.8 minutes, a real consideration for buyers weighing the drive to Dallas.

  • The town was surveyed in 1854 and named for an underground rock wall found while digging wells in 1851.
  • The county was carved out of Kaufman County in 1873.
  • Average rainfall is 38.68 inches a year, with July highs averaging 96 degrees.

sections.h2: What are MUDs and PIDs on a Rockwall tax bill?
sections.html:
They are special districts that can add their own charge to the bill. The appraisal district's home page offers two informational documents, one on municipal utility districts and one on public improvement districts.

If your neighborhood sits in a district, the extra levy shows up as a separate line on the statement. A buyer's agent will look for it, because it raises the carrying cost of the home. Ask the appraisal district which special districts cover your address and request the current balance before you list.

sections.h2: How are unpaid Rockwall taxes handled when I sell?
sections.html:
A lien for each year's tax attaches on January 1, and it stays with the house through a sale. The owner on that January 1 date can still be sued for the year's tax after transferring the property.

At closing, the title company requests a payoff from the appraisal district and sends it from your proceeds. The deed is then recorded with the county clerk, where the state manual lists a $5.00 first-page fee and $4.00 for each extra page. If the property is inherited, the heirs of a homestead can file an affidavit of ownership interest with the appraisal district to qualify for the homestead exemption.

Owners in Rockwall who are behind on taxes and want a fast answer can ask for a written cash offer that nets out the tax payoff.

faqs.q: Who do I pay my Rockwall property taxes to?
faqs.a: You pay the Rockwall Central Appraisal District, which collects for all entities on one bill. The county tax office page says this arrangement began October 1, 2012, and statements can be viewed on the district's payment portal.

faqs.q: When do Rockwall property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: They become delinquent on February 1 if unpaid by January 31. A six percent penalty and one percent interest apply at once, and the penalty grows to 12 percent by July 1.

faqs.q: Is it free to file a homestead exemption in Rockwall?
faqs.a: Yes. The appraisal district states that filing is free and warns owners not to pay solicitors who charge a fee. File before May 1 for the general exemption.

faqs.q: Why is Rockwall County so small?
faqs.a: It was formed in 1873 from Kaufman County, which was too far for residents of the northern area to reach easily. It covers 147 square miles, making it the smallest county in Texas, and Rockwall has been its seat since the start.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Rockwall house if the taxes are past due?
faqs.a: Yes. The back taxes, penalties and interest are paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Get a payoff statement from the appraisal district first so you know the exact amount.
